key_insight: FL4N introduces a feed-forward approach to rendering dynamic scenes from new viewpoints and at different times using a unified latent representation rather than explicit 4D Gaussian primitives.
problem_solved: Reconstructing a dynamic scene from monocular input requires understanding both 3D structure and motion. Existing feed-forward approaches based on explicit 4D Gaussians can suffer from temporal inconsistency and severe rendering artifacts.
method: Use a feed-forward model for 4D novel view synthesis.
Encode a 4D scene prior in a unified latent representation instead of explicit 4D primitives.
Target synthesis across both viewpoints and timestamps; further architectural details are not provided in the truncated abstract.
impact: FL4N offers practitioners an alternative representation for dynamic-scene rendering that aims to address limitations of explicit Gaussian methods. The supplied abstract does not include results confirming quality or efficiency gains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular input → unified 4D latent representation → novel-view, novel-time renderings.
Space-time grid showing camera viewpoints along one axis and timestamps along the other.
Conceptual comparison of explicit Gaussian primitives versus a unified latent scene representation.
Paired icons highlighting the two core challenges: 3D structure and temporal motion.
paper_title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko
